subject: Clarifying output rights vs training consent — Crescendo order form redlines
messages:
From: Annika Berg <a.berg@crescendohealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Bryce Holt <bryce.holt@crescendohealth.com>, Crescendo Legal <legal@crescendohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Crescendo draft order form — redlines on output & training clauses

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our legal redlines to the MSA + order form. Two items we want to highlight up front so we can avoid back-and-forth:

1) Output ownership: we require a carveout for clinical outputs that are derived from our patient data (Exhibit A). We propose a limited, nonexclusive license to use model outputs for internal analytics only.
2) Training consent / feedback: we cannot allow training on any customer-provided data or feedback without explicit, opt-in consent per dataset. We added a clause that requires written consent for retraining and a 30-day notice and deletion option.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the proposed carveouts or provide alternative language that preserves our confidentiality and regulatory obligations.

I attached the redline PDF and included Bryce (product/security lead) and legal. Happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Annika
Annika Berg
Director, Partnerships — Crescendo Health

Team — looping you in. Crescendo has sent redlines focused on two things: (A) output ownership carveout for clinical outputs, (B) a hard prohibition on training with customer data/feedback without explicit opt-in.

Quick asks:
- Monica / Laura: can Legal Ops / Contracts propose a compromise that is workable operationally? We want to avoid an outright rejection if we can offer a bounded license that addresses their regulatory needs.
- Jordan: sales would like to know if we have flexibility on an "internal analytics" license vs full assignment. If not, we may need to propose a fallback (time-limited license + opt-in training addendum).

I attached my quick summary (Redlines_summary_Rishi_v1.docx). I'll propose a 30-min legal+sales sync tomorrow if that helps.

Rishi

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:32:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Crescendo draft order form — redlines on output & training clauses

Rishi / all — thanks for the summary. I reviewed Crescendo's redlines and drafted alternative language that aims to split the difference while remaining operationally enforceable. Highlights: 

- Output rights: propose language that grants Crescendo exclusive rights to "Customer-Identified Clinical Outputs" as defined in Exhibit A for the limited purpose of clinical decision support and internal analytics; Redwood retains the right to use non-PHI-derived aggregated model improvements and telemetry for platform improvements, subject to strict de-identification and the exclusions in Exhibit A.

- Training & feedback: propose an opt-in training addendum: training requires an executed Addendum with explicit dataset scoping, time-bound duration, and customer confirmation that data has been deidentified to our mutual standard. We include a 30-day deletion notice after training and a certification requirement.

I attached the redline markup of the order form and a snapshot of our SOC2 evidence we can share with customers to build trust (SOC2_snapshot_20260930.txt). If Crescendo is agreeable to the addendum model, we can keep the order form language and move the implementation details to the addendum to avoid blocking procurement.

Suggested next step: 30-minute call Thursday 10/1 to resolve remaining definitions (what qualifies as "Customer-Identified Clinical Outputs").

Monica Patel
Contracts & Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
(attachment: SOC2_snapshot_20260930.txt, attachment: redline_orderform_monika_20260929.pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 16:35:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Crescendo draft order form — redlines on output & training clauses

Thanks everyone — good progress. Monica, your addendum approach sounds reasonable and is consistent with our playbook: keep the Order Form lean, move operational commitments to a tightly scoped addendum.

Two pragmatic asks before we commit to that path: 

1) Evidence & controls: ask Crescendo for a short checklist confirming the type of data that will be used (PHI? pseudonymized? clinical text?) and confirm SOC2 + encryption-in-transit/storage. If they are unwilling to provide that, we should require a technical review and a tighter isolation requirement on the dedicated capacity side.

2) Escalation path: Laura, please prepare a 1-page note for escalation to Legal Counsel if Crescendo insists on assignment/ownership language. Include expected business impact and possible concessions (one-year exclusivity, revenue-share, or usage-limited assignment) so Sales can evaluate.

Annika / Crescendo team — can you confirm availability for the Thurs 10/1 10:30am PT call or suggest a time? Also, attaching a DocuSign link for the standard order form — if we can agree to the addendum approach, we can proceed with a redlined addendum attached via DocuSign to avoid procurement delays.

Jordan Blake
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
